query: Create a task called 'Fix login bug' assigned to Chris Christoff in the Outgoing Tasks project
expected_behavior: Runs asana tasks create with -n, -a, and -p flags
Does not trigger interactive prompts
Reports the created task URL

query: Add Tom McFarlin as a follower to task 1234567890 and set the due date to next Friday
expected_behavior: Runs asana tasks update with task ID, -f and -d flags
Resolves 'next Friday' to a YYYY-MM-DD date
Reports the updated task

query: What sections are in the Lindris project?
expected_behavior: Runs asana projects sections Lindris
Displays the list of sections

query: asana tasks create is failing with 'unknown flag: --name'
expected_behavior: Identifies the user is running upstream v1.2.0
Suggests rebuilding from ~/Code/asana-cli
Provides the go build command
Confirms with the user before deleting
Runs asana tasks delete 9876543210
Reports success

query: Create a task called 'Fix the login bug' in the Lindris project assigned to David
expected_behavior: Attempts the create with -a "David" (or looks the name up first with asana users list -q David)
Recognises that the name matches several people — the CLI errors with 'user "David" is ambiguous' and lists the candidates
Does NOT pick a candidate, and does NOT retry with an arbitrary full name
Does NOT fall back to the MCP connector to bypass the ambiguity check
Relays the candidate names/emails to the user and asks which David was meant
Reports that no task was created

query: I moved all the tasks out of the 'Q3 2026 Rocks - Ben' section in Lindris. Remove the empty section heading.
expected_behavior: Uses asana projects sections delete Lindris "Q3 2026 Rocks - Ben" (with --yes when non-interactive)
Passes the full section name or its ID rather than a prefix like "Q3 2026 Rocks", which is ambiguous across seven sections
Does NOT reach for the raw REST API or the MCP connector — the CLI has a delete subcommand as of v3.6.0
If the section still holds tasks, relays the refusal and the task count instead of passing --force unasked
